skill.name: ena-database
skill.description: Access European Nucleotide Archive APIs and download paths for nucleotide sequences, raw reads, assemblies, taxonomy, and metadata.
skill.summary: Query ENA records, retrieve sequence metadata, and plan bioinformatics downloads from public archive endpoints.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from documentation examples that call documented public ENA endpoints or from Markdown code fences. The only confirmed issue is guidance to use plaintext FTP for bulk downloads, which has transport security limitations even for public scientific data.

remediation.issue: Plain FTP is recommended for bulk downloads.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer HTTPS or Aspera when available, and require checksum verification for files retrieved through FTP mirrors.

remediation.issue: Example URLs interpolate accessions and taxonomy values directly.
remediation.suggestion: Document that user-supplied accession, organism, and checksum values should be URL encoded before request construction.

content.value_statement: Finding sequence records across ENA can require several APIs and download methods. This skill gives Claude and coding agents a focused reference for searches, metadata retrieval, taxonomy lookup, and bulk download planning.
actual_capabilities: Explains ENA data types such as studies, samples, runs, assemblies, sequences, analyses, and taxonomy records.
Provides Portal API search patterns for metadata queries across ENA result types.
Shows Browser API retrieval patterns for XML, text, FASTA, links, and accession records.
Documents taxonomy, cross-reference, and CRAM reference registry endpoints.
Guides bulk download planning with FTP, Aspera, enaBrowserTools, checksums, and rate limits.
Includes retry and pagination guidance for reliable API use.
limitations: It is a documentation skill and does not include executable tooling or a packaged client library.
It depends on public ENA endpoint availability, rate limits, and response formats.
FTP download guidance may need stronger transport and checksum controls in regulated environments.
It does not perform downstream sequence analysis after data retrieval.

use_cases.title: Retrieve run metadata for a study
use_cases.description: Find samples, experiments, and run accessions for a known project before downloading FASTQ files.

use_cases.title: Build reproducible dataset manifests
use_cases.description: Collect accession IDs, file sizes, checksums, and download paths for workflow inputs.

use_cases.title: Explore organism-specific assemblies
use_cases.description: Search ENA assemblies and taxonomy records for a species or taxonomic subtree.

prompt_templates.title: Find records for an accession
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ENA database skill to explain which ENA API I should use for accession ERR123456 and what metadata I can retrieve.

prompt_templates.title: Search samples in a study
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ENA database skill to design a Portal API query that lists samples for study PRJNA123456 with accession, title, and collection date fields.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a FASTQ download manifest
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ENA database skill to outline how to get FASTQ download URLs, file sizes, and MD5 checksums for run ERR123456.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a large ENA workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ENA database skill to design a rate-limited workflow that searches assemblies for tax_tree(562), paginates results, caches taxonomy lookups, and verifies downloads.

output_examples.input: Find metadata for a sample accession.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend the Browser API XML endpoint for direct accession retrieval and explain when to request links or tabular metadata instead.

output_examples.input: Prepare downloads for a sequencing run.
output: Use the file report endpoint for run metadata.
Request FASTQ paths, MD5 checksums, and byte sizes.
Use bulk transfer tools for large files and verify checksums.

output_examples.output: The skill would point to the Portal API assembly result type and taxonomy query operators such as tax_tree for descendant searches.

best_practices: Request only the fields needed for a workflow to reduce response size.
Respect ENA rate limits and use retry backoff for 429 or server errors.
Verify downloaded files with published checksums before using them in analysis.
anti_patterns: Do not iterate API downloads for very large datasets when bulk transfer tools are available.
Do not parse XML responses with regular expressions.
Do not publish analyses without recording the ENA accessions used.

faq.question: Does this skill download ENA data directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides API and download guidance that Claude or an agent can use to build retrieval steps.

faq.question: Which ENA API should I use for search?
faq.answer: Use the Portal API for metadata searches across result types such as sample, study, read_run, and assembly.

faq.question: Which ENA API should I use for one accession?
faq.answer: Use the Browser API when you already know the accession and need XML, FASTA, text, or linked records.

faq.question: Can it help with FASTQ files?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes how to find FASTQ paths, sizes, checksums, and bulk download options.

faq.question: Does it cover taxonomy lookup?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents taxon ID, scientific name, and submission suggestion endpoints.

faq.question: Is FTP required?
faq.answer: No. FTP is documented for ENA mirrors, but HTTPS or Aspera plus checksum verification is safer when available.
